assumptions: Price-affine quasilinear utility with a common negative price coefficient
Invariant tastes and marginal costs across ownership scenarios
metadata.comparison: Firms 0 and 1 merge at fitted incumbent marginal costs; all products and consumer types remain available

equations.consumer_surplus: CS_t = sum_i w_i log(1 + sum_j exp(delta_jt + sigma_x nu_i x_jt))/(-beta_p)
equations.utility: u_ijt = beta_0 + beta_p p_jt + (beta_x + sigma_x nu_i)x_jt + xi_jt + epsilon_ijt

metadata.equilibrium_selection: PyBLP price iteration from observed prices at fitted marginal costs, with saved profit first-order and curvature checks
metadata.estimand: Population-weighted equilibrium consumer, producer and social surplus after ownership consolidation
metadata.identification: Demand moments use own cost shifter and rival characteristic/cost sums; supply moments use own and rival characteristics. The synthetic shifters are independent of demand and cost shocks.
metadata.normalization: Outside deterministic utility equals zero; epsilon is standard extreme value; nu is standard normal

beta_0.source: joint PyBLP demand and supply GMM

gamma.meaning: marginal-cost intercept and excluded cost-shifter slope

sigma_x.meaning: standard deviation of the taste coefficient for x

taste_distribution.meaning: standard normal nu; seven-node product quadrature

metadata.population: 140000 potential consumers in 80 independently generated four-product markets
metadata.scenario: Merge firms 0 and 1 in every market; recompute all four product prices and shares
metadata.welfare_definition: Expected log-sum consumer surplus plus variable profit, population-weighted by the same M_t in each scenario; no taxes, fixed costs or adjustment costs in this specification
